Since I'm having trouble with the search tools, let me approach this problem using chemical principles:

The acidity of haloacetic acids (XCH₂COOH) is influenced by the electronegativity of the halogen (X). A more electronegative halogen will pull electron density away from the carboxylic acid group more strongly, stabilizing the carboxylate anion and making the acid stronger (lower pKa).

The electronegativity of the halogens decreases in this order:
F > Cl > Br > I

Therefore, the acidity of these haloacetic acids would decrease in this order:
FCH₂COOH (most acidic) > ClCH₂COOH > BrCH₂COOH > ICH₂COOH (least acidic)

This is supported by their approximate pKa values:
- FCH₂COOH (fluoroacetic acid): pKa ≈ 2.66
- ClCH₂COOH (chloroacetic acid): pKa ≈ 2.87
- BrCH₂COOH (bromoacetic acid): pKa ≈ 2.90
- ICH₂COOH (iodoacetic acid): pKa ≈ 3.18

The least acidic compound is the one with the highest pKa value, which is ICH₂COOH.
